_comment: Edit this file to add gallery items. Each item: id, book, category (photography|painting|literature|object), title, date, source, url (page URL), image_url (direct .jpg/.png for tag), credit, description, location_ref (POI id or empty). Notes: Yasaka Pagoda item is CC-BY 2.0 (requires attribution). Osaka 1930s scans are low-resolution (~400–530px). Literature items are document pages — use 'url' to link out, no image_url.

items.title: Marunouchi 'London Street', looking toward the Imperial Palace
items.description: Babasaki Street's row of Western brick office blocks nicknamed 'London Street' -- the commercial and financial heart of Taisho-era Tokyo. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Marunouchi after the Great Kantō Earthquake
items.credit: Unknown / public domain — scan from Mainichi 'Shōwa History Vol. 4'
items.description: Marunouchi in the immediate aftermath of the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake. The Marunouchi Building (Marubiru), one of Japan's first large-scale office buildings, opened the same year. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building, entrance hall
items.description: The red-brick Tokyo Station at the foot of Marunouchi, completed 1914 -- the gateway to the capital's central business district. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: The Ginza, looking north — 'the most important thoroughfare in Tokyo'
items.credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division — no known restrictions
items.description: A stereocard view of the Ginza in late-Meiji Tokyo -- the city's most Westernized commercial boulevard, known for its brick buildings and electric streetcars. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Crowded Tokyo street near the train station (Admiral Tōgō celebration)
items.credit: Underwood & Underwood / Library of Congress — public domain
items.description: A Meiji Tokyo street crowded for a public celebration, photographed around 1905. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Gakushūin (Peers' School) girls' division at Yasukuni Shrine
items.description: Gakushuin, the Peers' School in Mejiro -- an elite institution reserved for children of the aristocracy, with separate boys' and girls' divisions. The photo is later than the novel's Taisho-era setting; the institution and its atmosphere remained the same. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Nara, temple district (Plate 28, 'Sights and Scenes in Fair Japan')
items.description: A 1914 collotype of Nara by master photographer Kazumasa Ogawa, made contemporaneously with the novel's Taisho-era setting. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Five-story pagoda and Sarusawa Pond, Nara
items.credit: New York Public Library — public domain
items.description: Kofukuji's five-story pagoda reflected in Sarusawa Pond -- the classic Nara vista. Kofukuji was founded in 710 CE as the family temple of the Fujiwara clan. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Hōkan-ji Yasaka Pagoda, Higashiyama, Kyoto (hand-coloured lantern slide)
items.description: The Yasaka Pagoda in Kyoto's Higashiyama district -- a five-story pagoda of Hokanji temple, one of the oldest surviving structures in the city. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Tenjuan temple garden, Nanzenji, Kyoto
items.description: A raked gravel garden at Nanzenji -- a major Rinzai Zen temple complex in Kyoto's Higashiyama hills, founded in the 13th century. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Ise Shrine — Plate 22, 'Sights and Scenes in Fair Japan' (Kazumasa Ogawa)
items.description: A 1914 collotype by Kazumasa Ogawa capturing the hinoki cypress architecture of Ise Jingu, the holiest site in the Shinto religion, dedicated to Amaterasu, the sun goddess. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Dōtonbori, Osaka, in the 1930s
items.credit: Unknown / public domain — from Asahi Shimbun 'Glimpses of Nippon'
items.description: Osaka's Dotonbori entertainment district in the early Showa years, known for its canal, theatres, and neon signage. Low-resolution scan. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Shinsaibashi-suji, Osaka, in the 1930s
items.credit: Unknown / public domain — from Asahi Shimbun 'Glimpses of Nippon'
items.description: The Shinsaibashi shopping arcade in 1930s Osaka -- one of the oldest covered shopping streets in Japan. Low-resolution scan. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Japanese sailors practising kendo fencing aboard ship
items.credit: Bain News Service / Library of Congress — no known restrictions
items.description: Kendo practice in bogu (full armor) -- the protective equipment worn in competitive swordsmanship, including men (helmet), do (chest plate), and kote (gauntlets). Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Two boys in kendo dress
items.description: Young kendoka in full practice uniform and armor. Kendo was widely practiced in schools and youth organizations in Meiji and Taisho Japan. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Members of the Takanawa Fencing School ('The Fighting Man of Japan')
items.credit: Public domain — from 'The Fighting Man of Japan'
items.description: A formal portrait of a Tokyo kendo school and its members in the Meiji era. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Suruga Miho no Matsubara — Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, no. 24
items.credit: Utagawa Hiroshige, 1858 / Library of Congress — public domain
items.description: Hiroshige's woodblock print of the Miho pine grove on Suruga Bay with Mount Fuji beyond, from his Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, 1858. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Emperor Meiji Worshipping at Ise Grand Shrine (ukiyo-e)
items.description: An 1869 woodblock print depicting the Emperor Meiji's imperial procession to Ise Jingu -- an early Meiji-era ritual fusing imperial ceremony with Shinto observance. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Genji Monogatari Emaki — 'Takekawa' (Bamboo River) chapter
items.credit: Heian court painters, c. 1130 (Tokugawa Art Museum) / public domain
items.description: A section of the 12th-century National Treasure Genji Monogatari Emaki -- the oldest extant illustrated handscroll of The Tale of Genji. The painting style, called tsukuri-e, uses layered mineral pigments over ink underdrawing. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Genji Monogatari Emaki — 'Hashihime' (Bridge Princess) chapter
items.credit: Heian court painters, c. 1130 (Tokugawa Art Museum) / public domain
items.description: Courtly interiors and junihitoe (twelve-layered court robes) from the Genji Monogatari Emaki -- the visual world of Heian aristocratic life. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Genji Monogatari Emaki — 'Yadorigi' (Mistletoe) chapter
items.credit: Heian court painters, c. 1130 (Tokugawa Art Museum) / public domain
items.description: A high-resolution section of the National Treasure Genji Monogatari Emaki, one of the oldest surviving examples of Japanese narrative painting. Relevant to: Spring Snow.

items.title: Uemura Shōen — 'Flower Basket' (Hanagatami)
items.description: Nihonga painting by Uemura Shōen, 1915. A woman in formal dress carries a flower basket. Shōen was one of the leading painters of the Taishō era, known for her portraits of women in classical Japanese settings.

items.title: Uemura Shōen — 'Firefly' (Hotaru)
items.description: Nihonga painting by Uemura Shōen, 1913. A woman in summer dress sits beneath a hanging mosquito net in the warm dusk, holding a fan. One of Shōen's celebrated series of women in quiet domestic interiors.

items.title: The Shinpūren Rebellion (Kumamoto Uprising)
items.description: Yoshitoshi's 1876 print of the Shinpuren (Divine Wind League) Rebellion in Kumamoto -- a short-lived uprising of former samurai against the Meiji government's Westernization policies, particularly the prohibition on wearing swords in public. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Repression of the Shinpūren Rebellion
items.description: A contemporary painting depicting the suppression of the Shinpuren uprising by government forces. The rebellion lasted a single night in October 1876, ending in the deaths of most of the conspirators. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Shinpūren no ran — Attack on Major General Taneda Masaaki
items.description: A nishikie (color woodblock print) depicting the rebels' night attack during the Shinpuren Rebellion of 1876. Relevant to: Runaway Horses.

items.title: Klong (canal), native houses, Bangkok
items.description: Bangkok's network of klongs (canals) gave the city its old nickname 'Venice of the East.' This Rijksmuseum photograph shows wooden houses and boat traffic along a central canal, c. 1900. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, on the Chao Phraya River
items.description: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn) -- a Buddhist temple on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok. Its central prang (tower) rises 70 metres and is encrusted with Chinese porcelain and colored glass. One of Bangkok's most recognizable landmarks. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Wat Benchamabophit, the Marble Temple, Bangkok
items.description: Wat Benchamabophit, the Marble Temple -- built under King Chulalongkorn (Rama V) at the turn of the 20th century using Carrara marble imported from Italy. One of the last major temples built in Bangkok before the modern era. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Wat Pho, Temple of the Reclining Buddha, Bangkok
items.description: Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha) -- one of Bangkok's oldest and largest temple complexes, home to a 46-metre gold-leafed reclining Buddha and the earliest center of public education in Thailand. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: The Grand Palace, Bangkok
items.description: The Grand Palace in Bangkok -- the official residence of the Thai royal family from 1782 until the early 20th century, containing throne halls, government buildings, and Wat Phra Kaew within its walled compound. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Life on the Klongs (canals) of Bangkok
items.description: Laden cargo boats and wooden houses lining a Bangkok canal. The city's network of klongs functioned as streets, markets, and thoroughfares -- earning Bangkok the nickname 'Venice of the East' from Western visitors. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Khlong Somdet, Bangkok
items.description: A 1907 photograph of Khlong Somdet -- one of Bangkok's main commercial canals, lined with houses on stilts and boat traffic. The canal system was the primary means of transport and trade in the city well into the 20th century. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Morning at a jungle river, Southeast Asia
items.description: Dense tropical riverine jungle characteristic of central Thailand -- the landscape surrounding Bangkok and the Thai countryside in the early 20th century. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Benares architecture beside the Ganges
items.description: The stone ghats (stepped embankments) of Varanasi (Benares) descending to the Ganges, where Hindu pilgrims bathe, pray, and perform cremation rites along the riverbank. Varanasi is one of the holiest cities in Hinduism. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Wat Phra Kaew — Temple of the Emerald Buddha
items.description: Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha), within the Grand Palace compound in Bangkok. The temple's inner gallery walls are lined with 178 panels of Ramakien murals -- the Thai adaptation of the Hindu Ramayana epic. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Ramakien Murals, Grand Palace gallery
items.description: One panel from the 178-panel Ramakien mural gallery at Wat Phra Kaew in Bangkok. The Ramakien is the Thai version of the Hindu Ramayana, and the murals depict battles, demons, and divine figures from the epic. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Garuda — National Emblem of Thailand
items.description: The Garuda (Khrut in Thai) -- the mythological bird-vehicle of Vishnu in Hindu cosmology, and the national emblem of Thailand. It appears on royal seals, government buildings, and temple pediments throughout Bangkok. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Kali — Kalighat Painting, Calcutta
items.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art / CC0 public domain
items.description: A Kalighat patachitra -- a bold, flat style of folk painting originating in 19th-century Calcutta, made by artists near the Kalighat Kali temple. This image depicts Kali, the Hindu goddess of time and death. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Ajanta Caves — Buddhist Cave Murals
items.description: The cave temples of Ajanta in Maharashtra, carved between the 2nd century BCE and 5th century CE. The caves contain extraordinary Buddhist murals depicting Jataka tales -- stories of the Buddha's past lives -- and Bodhisattva figures in mineral pigment on plaster. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Manikarnika Ghat (The Burning Ghat), Varanasi
items.description: Manikarnika Ghat -- the principal cremation ground of Varanasi, on the west bank of the Ganges. Cremations take place here continuously, day and night, and have done so for centuries. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Imperial Hotel, Tokyo — Frank Lloyd Wright building
items.description: Frank Lloyd Wright's Imperial Hotel in Tokyo, completed 1923. Its distinctive Oya-stone facade and Mayan-influenced design is one of the notable works of early modern architecture in Japan. The building stood until 1968. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha, Fujinomiya
items.description: The main sanctuary of Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha in Fujinomiya -- the head shrine of all Sengen shrines dedicated to the deity of Mount Fuji, set in ancient cedar forest at the mountain's base. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Hokusai — Reflection in Lake at Misaka, Kai Province
items.source: Wikimedia Commons (The Metropolitan Museum of Art)
items.credit: Katsushika Hokusai, c. 1830–32 / The Met Open Access — CC0
items.description: Mount Fuji inverted in a lake at Misaka Pass -- from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series. The reflection renders the mountain as a perfect mirror image in the still water. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: View toward Mount Fuji
items.description: The view of Mount Fuji from the Gotemba plateau on the mountain's southeastern flank, in Shizuoka Prefecture. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn / The Decay of the Angel.

items.title: Mahāmayūrī Vidyārājñī Sūtra (Peacock Gold Sutra)
items.description: A protective Mahayana text centered on Mahamayuri -- the Great Peacock Wisdom Queen, a Bodhisattva depicted four-armed and seated on a peacock. The text contains dharani (protective spells) and a central parable of a golden peacock king who loses his protective power through forgetfulness. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Laws of Manu — Manusmṛti
items.description: The Manusmrti -- the foundational Sanskrit text of Hindu dharma, codifying caste duties, karma, and the ordering of lives. Composed between the 2nd century BCE and 3rd century CE. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: The Questions of King Milinda — Milindapañha
items.description: A Theravada text (the Milindapanha) recording philosophical exchanges between the Greek king Menander (Milinda) and the monk Nagasena on questions of karma, rebirth, and the nature of the self. Nagasena's lamp-flame analogy -- one flame lighting another without being identical -- is one of Buddhism's most cited illustrations of transmigration without a permanent soul. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: The City of the Sun — Tommaso Campanella
items.description: A utopian treatise by Tommaso Campanella, written while imprisoned by the Spanish Inquisition (1602). Describes an ideal city-state organized around solar worship, communal ownership, and rational order -- one of the key texts of early modern European utopian thought. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Almsgiving of St. Rocco — Annibale Carracci
items.description: Annibale Carracci's painting of St. Roch distributing alms to plague victims, c. 1595. St. Roch is the patron saint of plague sufferers; Carracci depicts him present among the sick, distributing coins on the steps below him. Relevant to: The Temple of Dawn.

items.title: Album of Illustrations for the Tale of Genji (hakubyō ink album)
items.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0 public domain — full download available
items.description: A 17th-century accordion album illustrating the Tale of Genji in the delicate 'white drawing' (hakubyō) style. Downloadable in full from the Internet Archive.

items.title: The Small Mirror of Genji (illustrated Edo digest of the Tale of Genji)
items.credit: Library of Congress — public domain, full PDF available
items.description: A brightly illustrated 17th-century digest of the Tale of Genji, fully digitized as PDF. Provides classical Genji manuscript pages connecting to the Heian world evoked in Spring Snow.

items.title: Genji Monogatari (Saga-bon style edition, vol. 49)
items.description: A digitized Edo-period printed edition of the Tale of Genji from the Smithsonian's open-access collection — a primary-source manifestation of the classical text underpinning Spring Snow.
